Consult Summary:
- Michael John, a 40-year-old male, presents with three days of diarrhea, associated mild abdominal pain, single episode of vomiting, mild appetite loss, and possible mild fever, without alarming features. 

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for three days.
- Symptoms: Diarrhea occurring 4–5 times daily, described as sometimes watery and sometimes loose; associated with mild abdominal pain, single episode of vomiting, mild appetite loss, possibly mild fever.
- No recent travel or dietary changes identified as a cause.
- No blood or mucus in stool.
- Able to maintain oral intake; continues to drink fluids.
- No use of over-the-counter medications or interventions yet for symptoms.
- No other associated symptoms or systems review findings mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (status noted as “probably had/have asthma”).
- Medication: Inhaler “Laxepro” (dose/route/frequency not documented; uncertainty about medication name noted).
- No drug allergies.

Social History:
- No history of recent travel.
- No mention of smoking, alcohol, or substance use.
- No financial or lifestyle factors discussed.

Family History:
- Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62 (timeline: ten years ago).

Physical Examination:
- No explicit examination findings or vitals documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or discussed at this time.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute self-limiting diarrhea 
  - Assessment: Diarrhea for 3 days, likely infectious or viral gastroenteritis; currently mild with no red flag features (no blood/mucus, able to maintain hydration, minimal systemic symptoms).
  - Plan:
    - Maintain hydration; continue drinking plenty of fluids.
    - Advise use of Dioralyte (oral rehydration salts, over the counter).
    - Dietary advice: Soft/bland diet (crackers, toast, boiled vegetables, mashed foods), avoid dairy, meat, eggs, and fish until symptom resolution for at least 48 hours.
    - Allow yoghurt (probiotic).
    - Escalation: Seek further medical attention if diarrhea worsens (>6–8 times daily), dehydration develops, blood appears in stool, or symptoms persist >1 week (will require stool sample and further evaluation).
- Issue 2: Asthma (historical, no acute complaints)
  - Assessment: No acute asthma symptoms reported.
  - Plan: Continue current inhaler as needed.
- General plan items:
  - Reinforced review of notes in the patient app if clarification needed.
  - Advised when to seek follow-up.
